questions.question: How many people could stand on the island of Manhattan at four to a square metre?
questions.explainer: Manhattan is 59.1 km², or 59.1 million m². At four per square metre that is about 240 million people, more than live in Brazil.

questions.question: Flying non-stop in an airliner at cruising speed, how many days would it take to fly once around the equator?
questions.explainer: 40,075 km at 900 km/h is 44.5 hours, which is about 1.9 days in the air.

questions.question: Eating one apple a day, how many years would it take to eat a tonne of apples?
questions.explainer: A tonne is a million grams and an apple about 180 g, so about 5,600 apples: a little over 15 years of an apple a day.

questions.question: How many people are alive today for every person who lived in the Roman Empire at its peak?
questions.explainer: The Roman Empire peaked at roughly 60 million people. Today's 8.1 billion is about 140 times that.

questions.question: How many PlayStation home consoles have been sold for every person in Japan?
questions.explainer: About 500 million PlayStation home consoles have been sold since 1994, and Japan has about 124 million people: four consoles each.
questions.source_title: PlayStation consoles have sold over 500 million units (VGChartz)

questions.question: How many years of a 15-year-old cat's life has it spent asleep?
questions.explainer: Cats sleep about 14 hours a day, which is 14/24 of their lives. Over 15 years that is about 8.8 years asleep.

questions.question: How many Earths placed side by side would it take to reach the Moon?
questions.explainer: The Moon is on average 384,400 km away and the Earth is 12,742 km across, so about 30 Earths would fill the gap.

questions.question: How many lengths of a football pitch could a cheetah run in one minute at top speed?
questions.explainer: At 110 km/h a cheetah covers 1,833 m a minute. A pitch is 105 m long, so about 17 lengths.

questions.question: How many bowling balls would weigh the same as an African elephant?
questions.explainer: A bowling ball weighs about 7 kg and a big elephant about 6,000 kg, so about 860 bowling balls.

questions.question: How many golf balls would it take to fill an Olympic swimming pool?
questions.explainer: A pool is 2,500 m³. A golf ball is 42.7 mm across, 0.0000407 m³, and balls pack to about 64%, so about 39 million golf balls.

questions.question: How many ping-pong balls would fit in a bathtub?
questions.explainer: A bath holds about 300 litres (0.3 m³). A 4 cm ping-pong ball is 33.5 ml, and balls pack to about 64% of the space, so about 5,700 balls.

questions.question: Working full time on the UK National Living Wage, how many years would it take to earn a million pounds?
questions.explainer: £11.44 an hour for 37.5 hours a week is £22,300 a year. A million pounds takes about 45 years.
questions.source_title: National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage rates (GOV.UK)

questions.question: Spending like the average American household, how many years would a billion dollars last?
questions.explainer: The average American household spent about $78,500 in 2024. A billion dollars covers that for roughly 12,700 years, back past the end of the Ice Age.
questions.source_title: Consumer Expenditures 2024 - U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics

questions.question: Buying a brand-new car every single day, how many years would it take to get through a billion dollars?
questions.explainer: A new car in the United States sold for about $49,800 on average in late 2025, so a billion dollars buys about 20,000 of them: one a day for 55 years.
questions.source_title: Kelley Blue Book: new-vehicle average transaction price, October 2025

questions.question: How many Olympic swimming pools of water did ancient Rome's aqueducts deliver every day?
questions.explainer: Rome's eleven aqueducts are usually reckoned to have delivered about a million cubic metres a day for a city of about a million people. An Olympic pool holds 2,500 cubic metres, so about 400 pools a day.

questions.question: How many bath towels could be cut from the cloth of the Bayeux Tapestry?
questions.explainer: The Bayeux Tapestry is nearly 70 m long and about 50 cm wide, around 34 square metres of linen. A bath towel is about 70 cm by 140 cm, so you could cut about 35 of them.

questions.question: How many grains of beach sand would it take to fill a 10-litre bucket?
questions.explainer: A grain of beach sand is about a third of a millimetre across, so a litre of loosely packed sand holds roughly 30 million grains. A 10-litre bucket holds about 300 million.
questions.source_title: Counting Sand Grains - Fred M. Haynes

questions.question: If the whole history of modern humans were squeezed into one year, how many days ago did the first cities appear?
questions.explainer: Our species is about 300,000 years old and the first cities, such as Uruk, appeared about 6,000 years ago: two percent of the way back, which on a one-year scale is the last seven days.
questions.source_title: The first of our kind: Jebel Irhoud - Max Planck Society

questions.question: How many Manhattans would fit inside the land of the Louisiana Purchase?
questions.explainer: The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 covered about 2.14 million square kilometres. Manhattan is 59 square kilometres, so about 36,000 Manhattans would fit.

questions.question: How many tennis balls would it take to fill an Olympic swimming pool?
questions.explainer: An Olympic pool holds about 2,500 cubic metres. A tennis ball is 6.7 cm across, about 160 cubic centimetres, and loosely poured balls fill about 64% of a space, so roughly 10 million balls.
questions.source_title: ITF Technical Booklet 2023 (ball size 6.54 to 6.86 cm)

questions.question: How many loads of laundry does an American family get through between a child's birth and their 18th birthday?
questions.explainer: The average American household washes about 300 loads of laundry a year. Eighteen years of that is about 5,400 loads.
questions.source_title: Saving Water and Energy through Clothes Washer Replacement - NRDC

questions.question: How many king-size beds would it take to cover the floor of the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles?
questions.explainer: The Hall of Mirrors is 73 m long and 10.5 m wide, about 770 square metres. A king-size bed is roughly 1.9 m by 2 m, so about 196 beds would carpet it.
questions.source_title: Palace of Versailles: Hall of Mirrors - Bluffton University

questions.question: At a camel caravan's pace, how many months would it take to travel the full length of the Silk Road?
questions.explainer: The Silk Road ran about 6,400 km from Xi’an to the Mediterranean. A laden camel caravan covered roughly 30 km a day, so the whole way took about 210 days, around seven months.

questions.question: How many times does a person laugh in a lifetime?
questions.explainer: Diary studies find adults laugh about 18 times a day. Over 80 years that is about 530,000 laughs.
questions.source_title: Martin & Kuiper (1999), Daily occurrence of laughter - Humor

questions.question: How many years of a lifetime does the average American spend watching TV?
questions.explainer: The American Time Use Survey finds people watch about two and a half hours of TV a day. Over an 80-year life that is close to 9 years in front of the screen.
questions.source_title: American Time Use Survey 2024 - U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics

questions.question: How many people could stand shoulder to shoulder on the arena floor of the Colosseum?
questions.explainer: The arena floor was an oval about 76 m by 44 m, roughly 2,600 square metres. At four people to a square metre, about 10,500 people could pack onto it.

questions.question: Ignoring the door and windows, how many one-dollar bills would it take to wallpaper a 4 m by 4 m room with 2.5 m ceilings?
questions.explainer: Four walls of 4 m by 2.5 m add up to 40 square metres. A dollar bill is 15.6 cm by 6.6 cm, about a hundredth of a square metre, so about 3,900 bills, or $3,900, would paper the room.

questions.question: How many Lamborghini Temerario supercars could a trillion dollars buy?
questions.explainer: The Temerario carries a US sticker price of about $387,000, so a trillion dollars buys about 2.6 million of them, roughly one for every person in Chicago.
